@graph.name: Pouch Case Packer
@graph.description: A pouch case packer is a top-load machine that groups filled pouches and places them into shipping cases, by robotic pick-and-place for high-mix lines or by controlled gravity loading for repetitive formats. TRF Industrial Automation packs pouches with TRFRapidpack, its robotic case packer, and TRFDroppack, its gravity drop packer. Your line setup and speed decide which one fits.

mainEntity.name: What Is a Drop Packer, and How Does Gravity Packing Work?

acceptedAnswer.text: A drop packer collates products above an open case and loads them through a controlled drop instead of picking each one with a robot. TRFDroppack uses this principle for pouches, pillow bags and other flexible packages. It fits when the pouch tolerates gravity loading and the pack pattern repeats, which keeps mechanical complexity low and removes robotic end-of-arm tooling from maintenance.

mainEntity.name: What Is the Difference Between a Case Packer and a Case Erector?

acceptedAnswer.text: A case erector forms an open case from a flat blank, and a case packer loads products into that case. TRF supplies case erecting only as part of an integrated solution: TRFOnepack erects, packs and seals in one machine, and end-of-line projects with TRFRapidpack or TRFDroppack include case forming and closing, so one partner answers for the flow from flat case to sealed case.

mainEntity.name: How Many Products per Minute Can a Robotic Case Packer Run?

acceptedAnswer.text: TRFRapidpack is designed for applications of about 100 to 200 products per minute, TRFOnepack for about 20 to 50 and TRFDroppack for about 20 to 500. TRF publishes application ranges, not machine speeds: actual capacity depends on the pouch, the pick tool or drop path, the pack pattern and the infeed, and TRF engineering validates it for each line.

mainEntity.name: How Fast Can a Case Packer Change Over Between SKUs?

acceptedAnswer.text: It depends on how different the pouches, patterns and cases are. On TRFRapidpack, product and pattern changes are recipe-based with reduced mechanical adjustments, so most switches happen in software. TRFDroppack is designed for standardized patterns, where changes are less frequent. During engineering, TRF documents which changes are recipe selections and which require a format part.

mainEntity.name: Can a Case Packer Handle Frozen or IQF Products?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, within the validated application. TRFDroppack lists IQF product bags and frozen food bags among the flexible packages it loads by controlled gravity, and frozen food is one of the focus industries for TRFRapidpack. TRF validates the pouch, the pattern and the operating conditions with real product. Downstream, TRFSubzero palletizes in areas below 32°F.

mainEntity.name: Can Case Packing Equipment Integrate With My Existing Palletizer and Conveyors?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Each TRF case packing platform can run standalone or integrate with conveyors, case handling, palletizing and intralogistics as one end-of-line system. TRFIntraflow carries sealed cases to a TRFCobot, TRFCompact or TRFSpeed palletizer, and interfaces with your existing filler, conveyors and palletizer are defined during project engineering. See end-of-line integration.

mainEntity.name: What Is the Typical ROI of Switching From Manual to Robotic Case Packing?

acceptedAnswer.text: There is no typical figure, because payback depends on your plant. The estimate compares the installed cost of the system with the annual savings: people packing pouches by hand on each shift, shifts per day, local labor cost, the output the filler gains when packing stops being the constraint and time saved at changeovers. A TRF Sales Engineer builds it with your data.
